transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-15
Start: 16:00 PDT / 23:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Lin (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Helen Park (Lakemont HoC), Ravi Menon (CTO), Lina Ortega (Platform Eng)

Auto-summary (ai-generated, might be noisy):
- Customer is evaluating Redwood for EU-facing policy enforcement for claims triage. Primary constraints are HIPAA overlap for clinical data in certain lines and EU data residency for policyholders in Germany/France.
- Key asks: region-locking for logs and control plane evidence; KMS key residency with potential escrow; log redaction at inference-level; per-tenant isolation guarantees for a multi-tenant SaaS deployment.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time, quick intros, I'm Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE owning Lakemont, and with me are Diego and Arjun on the technical side.
[00:08] Helen: Hi all, Helen here, head of compliance at Lakemont. We're mainly focused on making sure whatever inference solution we pick meets EU data jurisdiction and the bits where HIPAA intersects for our health-related claims.
[00:16] Ravi: Ravi, CTO. We're looking at an inference stack that'll sit behind our claims portal, expected throughput is medium, maybe bursty.
[00:22] Lina: Lina, platform engineer, I'll be hands-on for networking and logs.
[00:26] Diego: Great, quick agenda, we'll do a short qualify then go into hosting models and then logs/KMS detail, leave time for next steps. Sound ok?
[00:33] Helen: Yes.
[00:35] Maya: Quick qual questions — what part of the workload do you see as regulated? You mentioned HIPAA, is it full PHI or tokenized fields?
[00:42] Helen: It's mixed. Certain claim attachments are PHI, but most request metadata is personal data by GDPR. We want to avoid any cross-border leakage and keep audit trails for any access.
[00:52] Ravi: Also we have a multi-tenant product line where some tenants are EU-only, some global. We want to make sure logs and model telemetry for EU tenants never leave EU datacenters.
[01:03] Diego: OK that's helpful. On Redwood's side we have three primary deployment patterns — hosted API, dedicated reserved pools, and private/VPC or on-prem. For EU residency + HIPAA you could go dedicated in an EU region or private if you need stricter network controls.
[01:18] Helen: Can you clarify the difference for logs? If we run hosted, are logs ever routed to Redwoods control plane in US?
[01:25] Arjun: Short answer — hosted control plane metadata might cross borders for management, but payload handling and model inference can be region constrained. For strict EU-only auditing we'd recommend either Dedicated in EU with region-locked logging or Private (VPC) where control plane endpoints are in your VPC and you control egress.
[01:42] Helen: We saw mention of 'control plane evidence' in your docs — we need auditors to be able to verify request/response pairs and operator actions, but only for EU tenants. Can that be scoped?
[01:52] Diego: Yes, we support per-tenant log partitioning and can configure log sinks to route EU tenant artifacts to EU-only buckets. There's an important nuance: our platform-level audit trail is stored in the control plane; for Private deployments the control plane can be deployed in your VPC which keeps everything in-region. For hosted we can provide filtered exports but some metadata may be stored in our systems.
[02:14] Lina: When you say "per-tenant log partitioning" how is PII handled? We need redaction of names and identifiers before logs are stored.
[02:21] Diego: We have two mechanisms — first, automatic prefix/KV cache trimming and token masking which can remove or hash certain fields at the SDK layer, and second, a configurable log processor that can run regex-based redaction prior to writing to sinks. Admittedly, regex is brittle, so for structured outputs we recommend function-calls/structured output schemas to avoid free-text leakage.
[02:44] Helen: Regex brittle is our discussion point, auditors want deterministic proofs. Do you provide a proof-of-redaction log saying what was redacted and why?
[02:53] Arjun: We emit redaction events — metadata that says a redaction occurred (type, rule id), not the PII itself. That metadata can be routed to EU sinks as well.
[03:05] Ravi: What about KMS? We have a requirement that keys for EU data must be resident in an EU KMS with our org owning the key. Can Redwood integrate with customer KMS or HSM?
[03:15] Diego: Yes — Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations; for Dedicated we can do a bring-your-own-key where the key material remains with you and we call the KMS endpoint in EU. For hosted we have envelope encryption and bring-your-own-key options but we need to verify exact residency constraints.
[03:31] Helen: Key escrow is a potential ask — auditors may ask for escrow arrangements. How do you handle escrow?
[03:37] Maya: Escrow is usually a legal/ops arrangement; our standard is to support KMS workflows and key rotation. For escrow we can discuss an enterprise arrangement with our legal team — it's not off-the-shelf.
[03:48] Lina: Network pathing — our security team insists on no internet egress from inference nodes back to US. Is that achievable with Dedicated?
[03:56] Arjun: Yes, Dedicated in EU with VPC peering and egress controls can prevent calls from leaving the region. For private deployments it's even stricter since control plane sits in your network. One caveat: certain telemetry/backups need agreed retention, we can sign off region-scoped backups.
[04:16] Helen: About fallbacks — if Dedicated capacity hits limits during a spike what happens? We cannot have data for EU tenants failover to a US-hosted model.
[04:25] Diego: We have smart routing policies — you can configure regional-only fallback or allow cross-region fallback. For your constraints we'd set strict region-only routing and configure throttling/queueing and pre-warmed burst capacity so requests don't silently route out. If you need guaranteed availability above that, Private is recommended.
[04:44] Ravi: How granular is RBAC for auditors and operators? We need read-only auditor roles that can pull logs and request traces but not trigger model rollouts.
[04:53] Maya: RBAC is per-route and per-model, we support SAML SSO and attribute mapping to roles. Auditors can be granted a role that only accesses log viewers and evidence exports.
[05:02] Helen: Retention — regulators want 7 years for some records, but we want to avoid storing raw model prompts for that long. Is there tiered retention?
[05:10] Arjun: Yes you can configure retention tiers per-sink. For long-term retention we recommend storing only redaction-metadata and hashed references to the prompt, not raw prompts. We can also provide an export that proves existence without disclosing the prompt.
[05:24] Lina: Any options for on-the-fly tokenization before it hits logs? For example we hash policy numbers at ingress.
[05:31] Diego: Yes an SDK pre-processor can tokenise or pseudonymize fields. We also support a sidecar proxy approach if you can't change clients.
[05:39] Helen: Would that break model quality? We're worried hashing IDs might prevent certain checks in the model.
[05:45] Diego: It's workload dependent. For a lot of classification tasks you can use deterministic pseudonyms and include mapping only in your secure vault. For free-text summarization you'd want to keep minimal context while protecting PII; sometimes you run a two-step flow: first a PII scrubber, then the LLM.
[06:02] Ravi: Let's talk about evidence for auditors: they'd like tamper-evident logs and a chain of custody. Do you sign logs or provide WORM options?
[06:11] Arjun: We can integrate with object-store WORM policies and sign events. For Private deployments, you can enforce write-once policies in your own buckets; for hosted/dedicated we can coordinate retention and WORM flagging on your sinks.
[06:25] Helen: Are there examples of customers doing EU-only per-tenant partitioning?
[06:29] Maya: Yes though names omitted, we've worked with a few insurers and banks on per-tenant EU pipelines. The pattern is dedicated EU pools + EU sinks + customer KMS.
[06:40] Lina: About model artifacts — do embeddings or KV caches ever get written to shared storage in the US? We want assurances they live in EU.
[06:48] Diego: Embeddings and K-V cache are stored on the local serving layer and persisted to region-local storage for Dedicated and Private. For hosted there are multi-region variants; we can pin model artifacts to the EU region for your tenancy.
[07:02] Helen: What about de-identification proofs? Auditors sometimes want to re-run a redaction step and confirm no PII remains. Can Redwood provide a replay environment?
[07:12] Arjun: We can provide sanitized replays for audits: we replay with synthetic tokens substituted and keep an audit mapping hashed and stored with the customer KMS. The mapping itself would be customer-controlled.
[07:25] Ravi: Pricing tradeoffs — what's the delta between Dedicated EU and Private? Ballpark numbers?
[07:31] Maya: Dedicated is a reserved GPU pool model with a smaller platform fee; Private carries a higher initial setup and license, but gives you full in-region control. We'll follow up with a pricing sheet.
[07:40] Helen: One last technical ask — can logs be forwarded to our SIEM in near-real-time with the same region constraint?
[07:47] Diego: Yes, we support streaming to SIEM via syslog/forwarders in-region with TLS. We can also push to your S3/GCS equivalent in EU, and from there your SIEM can ingest.
[07:58] Maya: OK quick recap — Lakemont wants: (1) EU-only residency of inference and logs for EU tenants, (2) KMS residency with BYOK and escrow discussion, (3) deterministic redaction events and proof-of-redaction, (4) RBAC for auditors and region-locked fallbacks, (5) pilot/benchmark to validate latency and redaction. Next steps are for us to send security docs and for Lina to share infra diagram. Any additions?
[08:18] Helen: That's accurate. Also add a sample data flow illustrating pseudonymization.
[08:23] Lina: I'll share network diagram and SIEM endpoints.
[08:26] Maya: Great. We'll send SOC2, architecture note, and a draft pilot runbook. Diego will own the benchmark details.
[08:34] Ravi: Sounds good, thank you.
[08:36] Maya: Thanks all. We'll follow up with meeting notes and schedule the pilot kick-off.

Notes on transcription: there are a few mis-heard tokens (K-V cash -> K-V cache, Redwood Dedication -> Redwood Dedicated), filler words, and some overlapping talk between Lina and Helen around 02:21-02:40.
